source: Make a Mario kart style racer where players race on random maps by drifting and using items. players can pick up coins to gain slight speed increases, but getting hit by an item causes players to lose coins. Make a map in a mall, a map in a mushroom first, and a map in the clouds. For the items, make a throwable shell, a droppable banana, a mushroom that gives a speed boost, triple mushrooms that give a speed boost 3 times, a red shell that homes in on the target in front, and a lightning that strikes all enemies in front

image_prompt.text: Rails along the racing line that physically stop karts leaving the track - mall balustrades, mushroom stalks, cloud bank edges
Curved track elements closing each circuit back on itself
A wide starting grid of evenly spaced kart slots at the start line of each map
map one - a looping track through a shopping mall interior, past storefronts and escalators
map two - a track winding through an oversized mushroom forest
map three - a track in the clouds on floating platforms and narrow bridges

layout_placement.text: Evenly spaced grid slots so racers launch side by side
Lap and split detection around each circuit
Coins scattered along the racing line that give a small speed increase and are lost when a player is hit
Item boxes on the racing line handing out the shell, banana, mushroom, triple mushroom, red shell, and lightning

notes: Circuit Racing preset taken whole and applied to all three maps.
P4 added because three distinct maps were requested in one build; the handoff carries one shape, one theme, and one scale, so the mall interior in particular is under-specified.
Racing has no collectible or power-up option, so the coins and item boxes are free-text layout entries.

open_questions.ask: How long should a lap be on each track?
Is the mall track fully indoors, which needs interiors generated separately?
How many laps per race, and how many racers?

coverage_missing.ask: How long is a lap on each track?
Is the mall track fully indoors?
How many laps and how many racers?
Should all three maps share one art style, or does each get its own?

answers.ask: How long should a lap be on each track?
answers.answer: Keep each lap short, around 60–90 seconds for an average player, so races stay quick and replayable.

answers.ask: Is the mall track fully indoors, which needs interiors generated separately?
answers.answer: Yes, make the mall track fully indoors, racing through recognizable mall corridors, storefront areas, and open atrium spaces.

answers.ask: How many laps per race, and how many racers?
answers.answer: Use 3 laps per race with up to 8 racers, which is a standard, manageable Mario Kart-style race size.
